tools.name: rh_token_safety
tools.description: Stored safety read for one Robinhood Chain token (0x + 40 hex): sellability, launch flags with evidence, where the launch money went, and the move since PumpPill first logged it. Never triggers a scan. found=false means not yet indexed, not safe; the miss is queued for reading. deep=true means the e

tools.name: rh_ticker_resolve
tools.description: The ONE Robinhood Chain contract worth naming for a ticker: alive, $10K+ in its pool, not flagged HIGH or CRITICAL. Other contracts using the name come back as a count, never a list. found=false means nothing clears the gate, which is itself the answer.

tools.name: rh_deployer_record
tools.description: What one Robinhood Chain wallet has launched and how those went: tokens, liveness, liquidity, which crossed $100K. Factory and relayer wallets above the launch ceiling get no record, and so does a wallet with a single launch. No success rate is computed: the rows hold only what crossed.

tools.name: rh_flagged_recent
tools.description: Tokens whose latest scan in the last 30 days found HIGH or CRITICAL structural risk, with the findings named. Each is a finding with evidence, not a verdict on price and not an accusation. Shows what the current wave of bad launches looks like; never a list to trade against.

tools.name: rh_stock_pairs
tools.description: Memecoins quoted in TOKENIZED STOCKS on Robinhood Chain. Pass a stock symbol (NVDA, SPY, TSLA) for the trading, unflagged tokens quoted in it with liquidity and latest scan risk; omit it for every stock with a count. This pairing exists on no other chain.

tools.name: rh_chain_stats
tools.description: How Robinhood Chain measures from PumpPill's index, recomputed hourly with the method in the payload: tokens seen, forward-measured outcomes, how many doubled, 5x, 10x or crossed $100K, how many are stock-quoted. Quote computed_at, not the time you asked. Counts, not a success rate: entry is the mar

tools.name: rh_whale_wallets
tools.description: Wallets holding 10+ ETH or $50K+ in tokens, read as on-chain balances. Tiers by dollars held (mega, whale, mini, large); positions_top names each wallet's three largest holdings. tools.name: rh_wallet_record
tools.description: One Robinhood Chain wallet's holdings and trades off the chain's own feed. A sell's size is derived from the router's minimum-out, so it is a floor, never profit. Many addresses on this chain are routing contracts, not people.

tools.name: rh_early_wallets
tools.description: Robinhood Chain wallets whose first buy landed in the early window of tokens that later crossed $100K, with the feed's base rate (meta.early_base_rate) beside every rate. tools.name: sol_early_wallets

tools.name: sol_token_detail
tools.description: Any Solana token by mint (base58): holders, bundled-launch read, what the deployer still holds, socials, and meta.verdict, one sentence on whether it trades, can be sold, what the dev holds and how far it has run. Start from the verdict; the rest is evidence. A clean read is not a reason to buy.

tools.name: outcomes_measured
tools.description: Forward-measured outcomes across both chains: the share of logged tokens that doubled, reached 5x, 10x, or never moved. tools.name: membership_status

tools.name: search
tools.description: Find PumpPill's read for a query: a Robinhood Chain address (0x + 40 hex), a Solana mint (base58), or a ticker such as HOOD. Returns ids for fetch. tools.name: fetch
tools.description: Fetch one result by the id search returned (rh:<address> or sol:<mint>). Returns the stored read as text with its citation and as-of time. Never triggers a scan; a missing read says so.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: x_chatter · Private data: rh_token_safety, rh_deployer_record, rh_flagged_recent, rh_stock_pairs, rh_chain_stats, rh_whale_wallets, rh_wallet_record, rh_early_wallets, sol_early_wallets, sol_token_detail, outcomes_measured, exit_check, rh_scan_now, premium_calls_recent, my_watched_wallets, x_chatter · Public sink: rh_chain_stats, outcomes_measured, exit_check, rh_scan_now, premium_calls_recent, my_watched_wallets, x_chatter · Destructive: sol_token_detail, rh_scan_now.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: x_chatter · Private data: rh_token_safety, rh_deployer_record, rh_flagged_recent, rh_stock_pairs, rh_chain_stats, rh_whale_wallets, rh_wallet_record, rh_early_wallets, sol_early_wallets, sol_token_detail, outcomes_measured, exit_check, rh_scan_now, premium_calls_recent, my_watched_wallets, x_chatter · Public sink: rh_chain_stats, outcomes_measured, exit_check, rh_scan_now, premium_calls_recent, my_watched_wallets, x_chatter · Destructive: sol_token_detail, rh_scan_now

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
